sections.h2: Why do Hamblen County's size and economy matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Hamblen County packs a lot into a small footprint. At 176 square miles it ranks third-smallest in Tennessee by land, and life centers on Morristown, the seat and biggest city. The General Assembly built it in 1870 from pieces of Jefferson, Grainger and Hawkins counties and named it for early settler Hezekiah Hamblen. Its courthouse dates to 1874.

Part of Cherokee Lake, a TVA reservoir created during World War II, reaches into the county, and Panther Creek State Park lies within its borders. Interstate 81, US 11E and US 25E cross it. Several large industrial parks on the east, west and south sides house manufacturers, and Walters State Community College has its campus in Morristown. Other named places include White Pine, Russellville, Whitesburg, Talbott, Lowland and Witt.

Census QuickFacts reports the following for Hamblen County:

  • 68,843 residents in July 2025, which is 6.7 percent above the 2020 base
  • 28,945 housing units, with 69.8 percent occupied by their owners
  • $210,900 as the middle value of an owner's home in the 2020 to 2024 period
  • $55,454 in household income and 14.8 percent of residents living in poverty
  • 258 permits for new construction in 2025

Greene County next door shows 77.1 percent, so more of Hamblen's housing stock is rented or otherwise not lived in by the owner.

sections.h2: Which Hamblen County offices deal with property tax?
sections.html:
Everything is in the Hamblen County Courthouse, 511 West Second North Street, Morristown, TN 37814. Assessor of Property Keith Ely, first elected in 2004, answers at 423-586-1852. His staff handles about 32,000 parcels carrying more than $3 billion in appraised value and builds the roll for Hamblen County and for the City of Morristown.

Trustee Scotty Long collects the money, on 423-586-6290. The Trustee is also the county's treasurer and banker, so every dollar the county receives passes through that office, and idle cash is invested to earn interest. A satellite counter at 2415 N Davy Crockett Parkway also takes tax payments. Fourteen commissioners set the rate and meet the Thursday after each third Monday at 5:30 p.m. The next meeting is November 19, 2026. Resolution 26-09, fixing the county tax levy for the fiscal year that began July 1, 2026, was on the agenda for the June 25 meeting. Ask the Trustee for the final county rate and whether Morristown adds its own tax to your address.

sections.h2: How does Hamblen County work out a tax bill?
sections.html:
The Assessor appraises, state law applies a ratio, and the rate does the rest. According to the Comptroller, the ratio is 25 percent of appraised value on homes and farms and 40 percent on commercial and industrial property.

Try the Comptroller's method on a Hamblen-sized home. Appraised at the county's $210,900 median, a house carries an assessed value of $52,725. Divide that by 100 for 527.25, then multiply by the rate on your notice. A rate of $1.00 would yield $527.25, and each extra dollar of rate adds the same amount. That rate is a placeholder, so use the real one from the Trustee.

The Assessor's office also runs reappraisal. After a countywide reappraisal, the Comptroller notes that a jump in value is not proof of an error and a judge may disregard it. The owner must still bring evidence of the right value.

sections.h2: When are Hamblen County property taxes due, and where do I pay?
sections.html:
Hamblen's tax page states that bills are due October 1 and become delinquent on March 1 in the next calendar year. The state calendar sets the start of payment at the first Monday in October, which was October 5 in 2026. With the date at November 15, 2026, the bill is open and no interest has started.

Where to pay, per the county:

  • At the Trustee's counter in the courthouse on West Second North Street
  • At the satellite office on N Davy Crockett Parkway
  • Online through TNPayments.com/Hamblen, a link that leaves the county site

Questions go to 423-586-6290. Businesses pay tax on equipment to the same office on the same calendar. The gross receipts tax goes to the County Clerk at 423-586-1993.

sections.h2: How can I contest a Hamblen County property value?
sections.html:
Phone the Assessor first. The office is also the contact for the local equalization board, whose five members the county commission appoints, and which sits once a year, beginning June 1. The state says an informal talk with an assessor can help but never counts as an appeal, so ask whether Hamblen offers one and still file with the board.

If the board's answer disappoints you, the State Board of Equalization accepts appeals filed by August 1, or forty-five days after the notice went out if that is later. An administrative judge hears the case and has 90 days to decide. The person appealing must prove the value. Scheduling goes through 615-401-7883, extension 2.

The state names the proof that tends to work:

  • Sold houses comparable to yours, adjusted for their differences
  • An appraisal, with the appraiser available to testify
  • A specific figure you propose, supported by facts about the house

You must also pay the part of the bill you do not dispute and any older unpaid years by the delinquency date.

sections.h2: Does Hamblen County have a tax freeze or relief?
sections.html:
It has both. The state relief program refunds part of the tax for low-income seniors, disabled owners and some veterans. In 2026 the income ceiling is $38,470 counting 2025 income, value is capped at $33,600 for refunds to seniors and disabled owners, and the veteran cap is $175,000. Applications go to the Trustee, who must receive them within 35 days of the delinquency date.

Hamblen is on the Comptroller's list of 28 counties with a freeze. It joined in 2007, and the 2026 income limit is $39,260. An owner who turns 65 by year end and meets the income test can fix the tax on a main home at the first qualifying year's amount. Each year requires a new application, and the fixed amount grows if the owner improves the property or moves to a different house.

sections.h2: What should I do about Hamblen County tax before I sell?
sections.html:
The Assessor's record date is January 1, but the title company splits the year's bill between buyer and seller at the table. Get the balance from the Trustee before listing, most of all for an inherited house or one with several unpaid years, because interest begins accruing once March 1 passes.

On its website the Clerk and Master, at 423-586-9112, keeps a delinquent tax section along with a tax search and payment tool. Once the sale closes, the deed is recorded in the Register of Deeds office inside the same courthouse, which also collects the state's recording taxes.

faqs.q: When are Hamblen County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Hamblen's tax page gives October 1. Bills turn delinquent the following March 1. Payment is taken at the courthouse counter, at the Davy Crockett Parkway satellite office, or through TNPayments.com/Hamblen.

faqs.q: Who is the Hamblen County property assessor?
faqs.a: Keith Ely, whose office is in the courthouse at 511 West Second North Street in Morristown. The number is 423-586-1852. The office values roughly 32,000 parcels.

faqs.q: Does Hamblen County have a property tax freeze?
faqs.a: Yes, adopted in 2007, with a 2026 income limit of $39,260. You need to be 65 by the end of the application year, own and occupy the home, and reapply through the Trustee every year.

faqs.q: How do I dispute my Hamblen County property value?
faqs.a: Start with the Assessor, then appear before the local equalization panel, which sits beginning June 1. A further appeal goes to the state panel by August 1, or forty-five days after the local notice if that date is later.

faqs.q: Where can I pay Hamblen County property tax online?
faqs.a: Use TNPayments.com/Hamblen, the link on the county's tax page. For balance questions, call the Trustee at 423-586-6290.
